ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The report to the 20th National Congress proposed the “seed industry revitalization action.” Rapeseed is an important oil crop. Screening breeding materials with excellent traits and exploring the corresponding genetic mechanisms are of great significance for creating new high-yield and high-quality varieties. Chinese scientists treated wild-type rapeseed (green leaves) with a mutagen and obtained a new-leaf etiolation mutant (yellowed leaves). The mutant was crossed with the wild type, and the results are shown in Figure Jia, from which it can be concluded that the recessive trait is yellowed leaves. Scientists cloned the gene causing new-leaf etiolation. Compared with the wild type, it has one base-pair change in the DNA sequence, causing a restriction enzyme B cleavage site to appear on the mutant gene (as shown in Figure Yi). Based on this, the experimental steps for detecting the F2 genotype are: extract genomic DNA→PCR→recover amplified product→treat with restriction enzyme B→electrophoresis. Question: How many electrophoretic bands should there be for the heterozygote in F2?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The report to the 20th National Congress proposed the “seed industry revitalization action.” Rapeseed is an important oil crop. Screening breeding materials with excellent traits and exploring the corresponding genetic mechanisms are of great significance for creating new high-yield and high-quality varieties. Chinese scientists treated wild-type rapeseed (green leaves) with a mutagen and obtained a new-leaf etiolation mutant (yellowed leaves). Scientists cloned the gene causing new-leaf etiolation. Compared with the wild type, it has one base-pair change in the DNA sequence, causing a restriction enzyme B cleavage site to appear on the mutant gene (as shown in Figure Yi). ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure Jia shows that the parents P are “wild type × yellowed leaves,” and all F1 show wild type; after F1 selfing, in F2 there are 980 wild-type plants and 346 yellowed-leaf plants, with a number close to 3:1. Figure Yi shows that the PCR primers are located at the two ends of the target DNA fragment, and the restriction enzyme B cleavage site is located inside the amplified fragment. Then reason: All F1 are wild type, and F2 is about 3:1, indicating that yellowed leaves are a recessive trait. The F2 heterozygote contains both one wild-type allele and one mutant allele. The stem states that the restriction enzyme B cleavage site appeared in the mutant gene due to one base-pair change, so the wild-type PCR fragment does not have this cleavage site and remains 1 complete fragment after digestion; the mutant PCR fragment has this cleavage site and is cut into 2 fragments after digestion. The PCR product of the heterozygote contains both the wild-type fragment and the mutant fragment, so electrophoresis can show 1 uncut long fragment and 2 cut short fragments, for a total of 3 bands.
